newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Ethical to raise 20 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ethical to raise 20 mln stg.

text.p: British-based drug development group Ethical Holdings Plc said on Monday that it hoped to raise around 20 million stg through its planned listing on the London Stock Exchange. In a telephone interview with Reuters, Ethical's chairman and chief executive officer Geoffrey Guy said "it is a coming home of a UK company and our story is particularly well understood in the UK" Guy founded Ethical in 1985 when biotechnology companies were obliged to look to the U.S. for funding. The group, which is listed on the Nasdaq exchange, has a market capitalisation of around $75 million.
"Being a small British company in a massive U.S. pond is very difficult. The main problem is visibility - getting your company in front of shareholders," said Guy.
He said Ethical had monitored the "dramatic changes in the London market" in terms of funding for biotechs over the past three to four years with a view to seeking a British listing.

Ethical, which has appointed Baring Brothers International Ltd as sponsor to the institutional placing and HSBC James Capel as broker, said its pathfinder prospectus would be issued in early June, with the listing taking place in late June or early July.
The company said it was keen to develop a base of shareholders in Britain and Europe, and could come back for fresh funds in a couple of years time.
Ethical specialises in developing drugs which are administered orally and via skin patches.

It launched a combination skin patch for Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) in cooperation with Schering Health Care Ltd in Britain in March. One of the group's problems in attracting U.S. investors has been that at present it has no products available on the U.S. market.

Guy said the group, which posted an operating loss of 2.7 million stg in the six months to February 28, had made a deliberate decision to move back to operating losses in order to fund pipeline development and focus on becoming a fully-integrated drug company, with its own manufacturing and marketing operations.
Ethical said it does not expect to return to profitability until 1999.
